card.name: Subject word before later-outcome verbs
card.fires_on: A noun or relative word such as patients, who, that or as, right after a group of people or a condition, where the next word is likely to be a time-ordered outcome like later, subsequently, eventually or developed.

modes.label: Patients who later developed
modes.description: The word patients or who after a treated group, just before a later-developing event such as MDS/AML or PML.
modes.example: The median duration of therapy with Lynparza in patients<< who>> developed MDS/AML was approximately

modes.label: Contact with an individual who
modes.description: The word who after a person exposed to or having an infection, in dosing-start instructions.
modes.example: within 72 hours following contact with an individual<< who>> has COVID-19.

modes.label: As it turned out
modes.description: Words in a phrase that hints at how things turned out later, in general news text.
modes.example: painfully accurate,<< as>> it turned out

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like later, subsequently, eventually and ultimately.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to say what happened to someone later on.
